aliases: Cocone (cone from base F to vertex c)

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Cocone `(F : J ⟶ C) := Cone (F^op). — "A cocone over F is the dual notion: a cone over the opposite diagram F^op, whose legs run F x ~> apex"

Class ACone ... (c : obj[C]) (F : J ⟶ C) := { vertex_map (x : J) : c ~{C}~> F x; cone_coherence {x y} (f : x ~{J}~> y) : fmap[F] f ∘ vertex_map x ≈ vertex_map y } — at F^op the coherence is the book's commuting triangles tau_j ∘ F u ≈ tau_i

ump_limits : ∀ N : Cone F, ∃! u : N ~> limit_cone, ∀ x : J, vertex_map[limit_cone] ∘ u ≈ vertex_map[N] — the limiting (universal) cone; at F^op (Colimit) this is the universal cocone mu : F -> Colim F through which every cocone tau factors by a unique t'
Definition colimit_med `(H : @IsAColimit J C F c) (N : Cocone F) : ... — the covariant restatement: the unique mediator Colim F ~> vertex of any competing cocone, alongside colimit_inj (line 135)

statement_record.book: A natural transformation tau : F -> Delta c, written tau : F -> c, is a cone from the base F : J -> C to the vertex c (all triangles tau_j ∘ F u = tau_i commute). A colimit of F is an object Colim F with a cone mu : F -> Colim F from the base which is universal: every cone tau : F -> c factors as tau_i = t' ∘ mu_i for a unique t' (the limiting or universal cone).
statement_record.intree: Definition Cocone `(F : J ⟶ C) := Cone (F^op). with legs vertex_map x : F x ~> apex and coherence fmap[F^op] f ∘ vertex_map x ≈ vertex_map y; universality is ump_limits at F^op, restated covariantly by colimit_inj/colimit_med in Structure/Limit/Preservation.v.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same: the cocone-as-natural-transformation-to-Δ and cocone-as-leg-family presentations coincide (the legs with triangle coherence are exactly the components of tau : F ⟹ Δc), and the universal-cocone property is the colimit ump verbatim, setoid-rephrased with ≈

Definition IsAColimit `(F : J ⟶ C) (c : C) : Type := IsALimit (F^op) c. — so the coproduct case is the instantiation of LimitIsUniversalProperty at C^op with the discrete two-object diagram, where ACone c (F^op) is a two-leg family (a ~> c, b ~> c), i.e. C(a,c) × C(b,c)

Proposition CartesianProductIsUniversalProperty : IsUniversalProperty C^op (fun z => IsCartesianProduct x y z) ... — the binary-product sibling instantiated explicitly, showing the specialization pattern the coproduct case follows by duality

statement_record.book: Objects a and b have a coproduct in C if and only if the functor c |-> C(a,c) x C(b,c) : C -> Set is representable (the representing object then being a + b).
statement_record.intree: LimitIsUniversalProperty (Structure/UniversalProperty/Limit.v:141): for any diagram F : J ⟶ C, IsALimit F c holds iff c represents ConePresheaf F, i.e. Hom(c,z) ≅ Cone(c,F) naturally; since IsAColimit F c := IsALimit (F^op) c, being a coproduct apex of the discrete pair (a,b) is representing the covariant cocone functor, whose value at c is the setoid of two-leg families (a ~> c) and (b ~> c) — C(a,c) × C(b,c) in substance.
